dateNote: Weights released July 27, 2026; July 16 was the hosted-model announcement.
subtitle: How memory changes across sequence length and model depth
summary: Kimi K3 combines channel-controlled recurrent memory with attention over earlier layer representations.
license: Kimi K3 custom license; review terms before deployment
lead: A deep language model moves information in two directions: across the tokens of a conversation and through the layers that transform each token. Kimi K3 changes both routes. Kimi Delta Attention manages sequential memory, while Attention Residuals changes how later layers combine earlier representations.

sections.title: Sequence length and depth are different axes
sections.html:
Picture a grid. Columns are successive tokens; rows are successive layers. Attention across tokens asks which earlier words matter to the current word. Mixing across layers asks which earlier representation of this same position remains useful. Both can involve weighted combinations, but they solve different problems.

The K3 model card specifies 69 Kimi Delta Attention layers and 24 gated-MLA layers within a 93-layer model. The schedule is 23 groups of three KDA layers and one gated-MLA layer, followed by one additional gated-MLA layer. [6] MLA means multi-head latent attention: it stores a compact representation for each previous token, so its cache still grows with context. Its 2.8 trillion total parameters include sparse experts, with about 104 billion active per token. The official announcement was July 16, but the downloadable weight repository began on July 27; this folder uses the weight-release date.

[1] [2]

The model therefore preserves both a recurrent route through token history and an attention route that can retrieve prior context. The size of the total parameter set tells us little by itself about either route’s context-memory cost.

sections.title: Forgetting can be selective within a memory
sections.html:
Kimi Delta Attention extends Gated DeltaNet with finer-grained, channel-wise gating. A channel is a coordinate of the internal representation, not a labeled human concept. The delta update corrects the association selected by the current key; the channel gates first control how much older state survives. The original Kimi Linear release predates K3. Its chunkwise algorithm computes groups of token updates efficiently without changing the underlying recurrence.

[3]

As an analogy, imagine tracking a meeting’s current speaker and the project’s deadline. At a speaker change, one part of the memory should change quickly while another should persist. A single decay knob weakens everything together. Separate gates allow different coordinates to retain information for different durations. The analogy motivates selective forgetting; it does not imply that a trained coordinate literally represents a deadline.

K3 adds a specific numerical change: its retention factor stays above exp(−5), about 0.0067, rather than approaching zero without a lower bound. The fast algorithm divides by products of these factors across small computation tiles of 16 tokens. Without a lower bound, a tiny product can make that division overflow the numeric format. The bound permits hardware matrix multiplication for this part of the calculation. It does not guarantee permanent memory: repeated factors below one still decay. [6]

The toy memory counts show why recurrence is attractive. A fixed-size state does not add one new entry for every new token. However, finite state must compress information, and the remaining MLA layers still have a growing cache. The whole K3 model is not constant-memory.

sections.title: Later layers can select earlier representations
sections.html:
A conventional residual connection adds a layer’s output to the representation already flowing through the network. Repeating this means that contributions accumulate along depth. Attention Residuals replaces fixed-weight accumulation with learned, input-dependent attention over earlier representations. The component paper also proposes block-level aggregation to reduce the memory and communication cost of keeping every intermediate output. K3 uses this Block AttnRes variant: it sums contributions within blocks, then attends to completed block summaries, the current partial block and the original embedding. Its report groups the 93 layers into eight blocks, with a partial final block. [6]

[4]

Use a numerical teaching example. Suppose three earlier scalar representations are 2, 5 and −1. Adding them gives 6. A normalized attention mixture with weights 0.2, 0.7 and 0.1 gives 0.2×2 + 0.7×5 − 0.1 = 3.8. The second operation can emphasize one source and diminish another; it is not the same operation as addition followed by a global scale.

The scoring query is a learned vector belonging to the receiving layer; its source representations vary with the input token. That is why the weights are input-dependent even though the query itself is a parameter. This is attention along depth. It does not replace attention between tokens. A layer may need both: retrieve relevant earlier words, then choose which level of processing contains the features needed for the next transformation.

sections.title: A larger model is also a systems design
sections.html:
K3 also uses Stable LatentMoE. Its selected routed experts process a 3,584-dimensional projection of the 7,168-dimensional backbone representation, while shared experts keep a full-width path. Normalization and bounded internal activations help control numerical growth before the routed result returns to the backbone. [6] K3 also uses a low-bit post-training and deployment recipe. The official model card lists 16 selected routed experts from 896, two shared experts, and quantization-aware training from supervised fine-tuning onward, with MXFP4 weights and MXFP8 activations. These are block-scaled four-bit and eight-bit floating-point formats; scale metadata and selectively higher-precision components add storage beyond the nominal bit counts. These choices address different costs and should not be collapsed into one efficiency number.

[1]

For a fair experiment, vary one mechanism while holding data, compute and evaluation fixed. A release comparison changes many ingredients at once. The component papers provide more targeted evidence than a flagship leaderboard table, while the released checkpoint demonstrates that the ingredients can be assembled into a working system.

The conceptual advance is a separation of questions: what should persist through time, what should remain retrievable, and which earlier layer representation should a later layer use? Each requires its own memory and computation accounting.
